summary: A new install's setup writes claude_permission_mode = "auto" into its new config.toml. Existing installs are unchanged.

replay.detail: No replay. The setting is read from config.toml when the daemon starts and when a Claude seat is created.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and fleet coordination are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Nothing changed for you if you run bypass today: a config.toml without claude_permission_mode reads as bypass, so new Claude seats still start with --dangerously-skip-permissions, and seats that already exist keep the arguments they were declared with. st never adds or rewrites the key in a config that exists, on upgrade, setup re-run, doctor, repair or service install and uninstall. A seat created with auto passes --permission-mode auto, needs Claude Code 2.1.283 or newer and a supported model, and is shown as not in the mode it asked for when Claude falls back to Manual.

downtime.detail: No restart is needed to keep the current behavior.

manual.detail: To move to auto on purpose, add claude_permission_mode = "auto" to your own config.toml and restart the daemon; st doctor then prints "auto: set in config.toml". One seat can differ with st agents new --claude-permission-mode auto|bypass.

recovery.detail: Remove the key, or set it to bypass, to return to the previous behavior; no stored data changes.
